q1: How much padel have you played?
q1a: None yet, or only a handful of times.
q1b: Less than 6 months, or only now and then.
q1c: 6 months to 2 years, about once a week or more.
q1d: More than 2 years of regular play.
q2: Have you played tennis, squash or another racket sport?
q2b: Yes, casually or a long time ago.
q2d: Yes, competitively — club team, leagues or tournaments.
q3: Rallying from the back of the court — which is closest to you?
q3a: I often miss or hit long; rallies rarely last more than a few shots.
q3b: I can rally at a gentle pace, but my backhand or faster balls cause errors.
q3c: I'm consistent on both sides at medium pace and can choose where I hit.
q3d: I control pace, depth and direction even under pressure and rarely give away easy points.
q4: When the ball comes off the back or side glass, what usually happens?
q4a: I try to hit everything before it reaches the glass, or I lose the point.
q4b: I can return a simple ball off the back glass, but side walls and corners beat me.
q4c: I return back- and side-wall rebounds consistently, usually with a lob or a safe ball.
q4d: I read double-wall rebounds early and can attack a ball coming off the back glass.
q5: At the net, what can you do reliably?
q5a: I rarely go to the net, or I miss most volleys.
q5b: Basic volleys when the ball comes to me; lobs over my head are a problem.
q5c: Solid volleys on both sides and a controlled bandeja to hold the net against lobs.
q5d: I place volleys with intent, use bandeja and víbora, and finish high balls with a smash.
q6: Which matches do you usually play, and how do they go?
q6a: Mostly lessons or casual hitting — I rarely play full matches.
q6b: Friendly matches with beginners and improvers.
q6c: Regular competitive club matches against intermediate players; I win about half.
q6d: Top club level, leagues or tournaments; I usually beat intermediate club players.
